subject: social
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

topics.topic: The Story of the Past and Evidences in History
covers: Explain what history is and how past events affect today
Talk with grandparents and record their family's history
Tell apart the ancient, medieval and modern periods of history
Tell archaeological sources from literary sources
Explain why old records and sources must be kept safe
Tell apart the work of a historian and an archaeologist
Compare the Gregorian and Saka calendars
Draw a timeline and mark AD (CE) and BC (BCE) on it
Put events in order and mark them on a timeline
Mark important dates on the school calendar
Make their own calendar using what they know about how calendars work
Explain civic sense and what a citizen is
Know why being a good neighbour matters
Show how to care for public and private places such as schools, hospitals, parks and monuments
Explain the role of elections and voting
Explain the role of a class monitor or prefect
Show respect for public property and suggest ways to look after it
Start to solve small problems in school and the neighbourhood
Explain the Earth's axis, rotation and revolution
Explain day and night, and the seasons
Name the four realms of the Earth: lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere
Identify major landforms such as mountains, plateaus, plains and deserts
Locate oceans and continents on an outline map of the world
Use signs, symbols, colours and scale on a map
Use scale and cardinal directions for mapping
Find their own state on the map of India
Locate the capital, important cities, rivers and landforms of their state
Describe the state's climate, seasons and vegetation
Name the main crops and farming of the state
Appreciate the state's cultural heritage, including its folk songs, dances and festivals
Name the major physical divisions of India, such as the Himalayas, Northern Plains and Peninsular Plateau
Locate major mountains, plateaus and rivers on a map of India
Name the major rivers of India and say which are perennial and which are not
Compare the food, festivals, languages and ways of life in different parts of India
Understand how land features affect where people live and how many live there
Recognise the things that unite people despite their differences

topics.topic: Pollution- Its Impact on the Environment
covers: Explain what pollution is and its causes, effects and prevention
Describe air, water and noise pollution with examples
Explain the ideas of reduce, reuse and recycle, and how to dispose of waste properly
Sort waste into biodegradable and non-biodegradable, and use dustbins for each
Understand why clean, safe water matters and how to save water at home
Suggest ways to reduce each kind of pollution
